title: Lockstep SOC2 prep: control mapping + risk prompts (scratch)
content:
Purpose / context:
This is a personal scratchpad for mapping Redwood-specific telemetry and artefacts to common SOC2 control areas. Not polished — stream-of-consciousness, questions, and a runnable checklist. Focus is on the parts that typically trip us up in Private/Dedicated deployments vs Hosted API (evidence variety).

High-level scope:
- In-scope services: Redwood Hosted API (public), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem package).
- Controls to cover: Access controls, change mgmt, logging/monitoring, key management, incident response, availability/SLA evidence, vendor mgmt for infra partners.

Quick mapping (rough, convert to table later):
- A. Logical access (user provisioning, role reviews):
  * Evidence: Okta user export + SCIM logs (hosted), IAM roles in customer VPC (private), internal IAM for dedicated cluster access (audit enrollments).
  * Where to pull: Okta admin console export (monthly), support tickets with access grants (JIRA tickets), internal 'access-grants' S3 (encrypted) — confirm retention.
  * Open Q: Do we have a consolidated monthly reviewer list saved somewhere? I remember a spreadsheet in shared_drives/company/misc but need link.

- B. Change management (code/config rollouts):
  * Evidence: GitHub PRs with approvals + release tags; release notes; deployment job logs (Argo/GHA); for Private: customer-specific package build manifests.
  * Where to pull: github.com/redwood-inference (repo), CI job IDs (GHA logs archived?), release-engineering ticket.
  * Note: For canary rollouts we also need canary metrics snapshot (latency/error rate) at time of rollout — saved to observability dashboard snapshots. Need to automate snapshot export.

- C. Logging & monitoring (integrity & retention):
  * Evidence: centralized logging (ELK/Datadog) config + exports, retention policy doc, sample logs for a date range.
  * Hosted specifics: request/response logs (redact PII) retained X days — find policy.
  * Private specifics: customer may host logs; we need our agent logs showing install/upgrade events.
  * Action: Confirm log retention windows for Hosted (prod) vs Dedicated (internal infra) vs Private installations — add to matrix.

- D. Key management / encryption at rest/in transit:
  * Evidence: KMS key rotation policy, HSM usage notes, key access control lists.
  * For Private: customers can use their own KMS — need proof of integration (KMS ARNs). For on-prem air-gapped: offline key-transfer SOP?
  * TODO: ask Infra-SE on 2/20 for a short narrative on how customer KMS is integrated and where KMS usage logs live.

- E. Incident response & forensics:
  * Evidence: IR runbook, simulation evidence (tabletop run notes), incident tickets with postmortems, timelines.
  * For Private: customer-owned environment — what handoff docs do we give? need template for joint IR.
  * Open question: Are we capturing packet-level captures in private installs? Probably not by default. Add to ops checklist.

- F. Availability & capacity (Dedicated reservations):
  * Evidence: reserved capacity contracts, autoscaling config, historical throughput metrics, SLA reports.
  * Where: finance contracts, dedicated dashboard snapshots, billing exports.

Evidence sources (draft list):
- Okta admin export (monthly) — owner: IAM team (Noah)
- GitHub PRs & release tags — owner: release-engineering (Jonas)
- CI/CD logs (GHA) export path — want archived links in ticketing system
- Datadog dashboards snapshots (per-release) — owner: observability (Ellie)
- KMS key usage logs (CloudTrail) — owner: infra (ask SRE)
- Support/PS onboarding docs for Private customers (customer-specific) — solutions-eng
- Dedicated contract PDFs + invoice history — finance/legal

Control evidence examples (raw):
- Change mgmt: PR #3457 merged 2026-01-12, release v1.42.3, GHA job 2026-01-12-334 exported link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rtd/actions/runs/2026-01-12-334 (archive?)
- Access review: Okta export csv (2026-01-31) s3://redwood-internal/access-reviews/2026-01-31.csv (confirm encryption)
- Incident: INC-2026-0301 (partial outage), postmortem draft in confluence ID: CONFLUENCE-3421 (need final sign-off)

Unresolved risk questions (high-priority):
1) Private deployments and evidence custody: auditors often want to see logs from the customer instance. We only retain agent-side evidence. Do we have a standard clause for evidence gathering in the Private contract? (Legal/PS)
2) Customer-managed KMS: auditors want to verify key rotation and access. How do we get time-bound proof (e.g., ARNs plus CloudTrail snippets) without storing customer secrets? Is customer comfortable sharing read-only CloudTrail extracts?
3) On-prem air-gapped installs: how to show build provenance/SBOMs for appliance images if the customer environment is isolated? Need documented chain-of-custody for image signing.

Quick action list (who/when):
- [Samira] Draft short narrative for auditors: "How evidence differs by deployment type" — due 2026-02-24.
- [Noah] Pull Okta export and confirm retention/where stored (s3 path) — due 2026-02-20.
- [Ellie] Create automated dashboard snapshot job for release canaries — prototype by 2026-03-05.
- [Jonas] List of PRs/releases for last 12 months with approver names (CSV) — due 2026-02-28.
- [Infra/SRE] Short note on KMS audit flow for Private customers (how to obtain CloudTrail snippet) — requested 2026-02-20.

Draft control narrative snippets (copyable to Confluence):
- "Access reviews: Redwood conducts monthly role entitlement reviews via Okta. Review artefacts are exported as encrypted CSVs and stored in internal S3 with restricted access. Reviewer list and sign-off timestamps are recorded in the Access Review spreadsheet (link)."
- "Change management: All production code changes must go through GitHub PRs with at least two approvers. Releases are tagged and CI/CD job logs are archived. For Private deployments, customer-specific build manifests and upgrade approvals are attached to the customer onboarding folder."

Evidence collection risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Evidence sprawl across s3, GH, Datadog, and customer portals.
  Mitigation: Create a "SOC2 evidence index" (single doc with links + snapshot copies) for each audit cycle. Owner: trust-ops.
- Risk: Private customers unwilling to share logs.
  Mitigation: Use signed attestations and agent-collected telemetry as supplement; include explicit evidence clauses in onboarding checklist.

Notes to self / random thoughts:
- Need a tiny script to snapshot dashboard -> PDF + upload to evidence-bucket. Might reuse existing observability tooling.
- Consider adding standard label/metadata on support tickets that are evidence-worthy (e.g., "evidence:true") so searches are simpler.
- Check with legal if sharing CloudTrail read-only extracts has any PII/TOS implications.

Meeting minutes (quick) — 2026-02-19 call with OBS/Infra
- Observability: can schedule snapshot job, will require service account with limited scope.
- Infra: KMS logs are in CloudTrail, retention 90 days by default; can extend to 365 for audit window but cost implications.
- Action: Ellie to prototype snapshot; Infra to estimate cost of extended CloudTrail retention.

Next steps (this doc):
- Convert mapping above into a simple CSV with columns: control, evidence, owner, artifact link, notes.
- Collect 3 sample artifacts per control to validate format requirement for auditors.
